subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should Browser upload continue supporting paths-only arm-then-later-click as a normal workflow, or should agent/tool flows be moved toward atomic upload-with-trigger behavior for dynamic pages?
rationale: Both paths-only arming and upload-with-ref are valid current behavior, so changing defaults or guidance affects the Browser API contract rather than only fixing a local implementation bug.

options.title: Prefer atomic while preserving compatibility
options.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer the existing upload-with-trigger path with regression and live proof.

options.title: Retire paths-only arming
options.body: Require a trigger ref, inputRef, or element for upload flows and provide migration guidance for callers that depended on delayed arming.

options.title: Document current recovery
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document stale-ref recovery plus selector/batch mitigations, accepting that the underlying flake can still occur.

recommendation.title: Prefer atomic while preserving compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer the existing upload-with-trigger path with regression and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining question is Browser bundled-plugin upload API direction, and the history points most strongly to this owner for that surface.
